caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The line plot illustrates the performance of different editing methods on BioMedLM in terms of accuracy (ACC %) as a function of co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," ranges from 10^0 to 10^3, indicating the frequency of co-occurrence. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)," ranges from 40% to 65%, representing the accuracy percentage. The plot includes six lines, each representing a different editing method: Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME. The Base line is marked with a black circle and remains relatively flat, indicating a consistent performance with a plateau at approximately 44%. The MEND line, marked with a brown diamond, shows a moderate increase in accuracy, reaching about 56%. The FT line, marked with a blue triangle, also shows an increase but is surpassed by IKE at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2, where IKE, marked with a red triangle, reaches approximately 52%. The MEMIT line, marked with a purple square, follows closely behind MEND, reaching about 55%. The ROME line, marked with a green square, shows the most significant increase, starting at around 51% and reaching approximately 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers.
